A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed an approach which is able to treat a large parameter regime, and which gives a good qualitative picture of the crossover between Fermi and Luttinger liquid behaviors.
we have shown that the Luttinger liquid picture is valid for weakly coupled chains, even though it is not a low-energy fixed point.
the Luttinger liquid description of the normal state in weakly coupled chains is not an artifact of the bosonization approximation but rather a robust feature of the physics of these systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Luttinger liquid description of quasi-one-dimensional metals is not an artifact of the one-dimensional approximation, but a consequence of the long-range nature of the Coulomb interaction.
, in the case of weak interchain hopping, the Luttinger liquid picture provides the most accurate description of the normal state of quasi-one-dimensional conductive materials.
, in contrast to the case of the one-dimensional Hubbard model, there is no contradiction between Luttinger liquid physics and the existence of a well-defined Fermi surface in higher dimensions.
